Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-'Ankabut (The Spider)

It is Meccan according to the view of 'Ata' and al-Hasan, and Madani according to one of the two opinions of Ibn 'Abbas. It is also reported from him in another narration that it is Meccan. Some of it was revealed in Medina and some of it was revealed in Mecca. It is reported from al-Sha'bi that it is Meccan except for the first ten verses, which are Madani.

It is reported from 'Ali that he said: It was revealed between Mecca and Medina. This is a strange (gharib) narration.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾. We have already explained its meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿Do the people think﴾. Al-hisbān (supposing) and al-ẓann (thinking) are close in meaning; it is the preponderance of one of two contradictories over the other. Doubt (al-shakk) stands between two contradictories, while knowledge (al-ʿilm) is a certainty that one of them exists.

And His saying: ﴿that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe"﴾. Its meaning: do they suppose that they will be content with them merely saying, "We believe"? And His saying: ﴿and they will not be tested﴾, meaning: they will not be afflicted. Mujāhid said: they will not be tested in their wealth and their persons. It is also said that its meaning is: they will not be commanded or forbidden, whereas God's testing of His servants is through commands and prohibitions.

Some of them said: God, exalted is He, first commanded people merely to have faith; then He imposed on them prayer, zakāt and the rest of the laws, and this was difficult for them, so God, exalted is He, revealed this verse. It is reported from al-Shaʿbī and others that he said: When the Companions of the Messenger of God emigrated, a group remained in Mecca who had believed but had not emigrated. Those who had emigrated wrote to them that God, exalted is He, would not accept their faith until they emigrated. So they emigrated, and a group of the polytheists followed them and harmed them, so some were killed and some escaped, and God, exalted is He, revealed this verse. It is also reported from some of them that the verse was revealed concerning ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿa, who had emigrated to Medina. His two maternal brothers, Abū Jahl and al-Ḥārith, the sons of Hishām, came to him and said: Our mother has sworn that if you do not return she will not eat or drink, and will not let shelter of any house cover her; and Muhammad commands kindness, so return with us. He returned with them, but when they were part of the way, they betrayed him, bound him, and brought him to Mecca, and each of them flogged him one hundred lashes. Then, when he reached his mother, she began to beat him with whips until he renounced his religion. So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse. His Islam was later made good.

And among the well-known and established reports: the Prophet (ﷺ) used to supplicate in the qunūt, saying: "O God, deliver Salamah ibn Hishām, ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿa, al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd, and the weak ones among the believers in Mecca. Tighten Your grip upon Muḍar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph." He supplicated thus (this way) for a month, then he stopped. He was asked about that, and he said: "Do you not see that they have come?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We certainly tested those before them﴾, meaning: We tried (ibtala) those before them, namely the prophets and the believers. It is also said: We tried the Children of Israel through Pharaoh, and likewise We tried every prophet with an enemy of his. It is indeed established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when his companions complained to him of what they suffered at the hands of the disbelievers: "Surely you are being hasty. Indeed, among those before you, a man would be sawn in two with saws, and that would not turn him away from his religion. And Allah will surely complete this affair."

And His saying: ﴿[So Allah will surely know] those who are truthful﴾, meaning: We will test them with a test of one who seeks to know their state. It is also said: "And Allah will surely know those who are truthful" means: He will know the thing as it actually occurs, and that is what He will recompense for. It was also said: "So Allah will surely know those who are truthful" means: Allah will surely make manifest the truthful from among the liars.

And His saying: ﴿[And He will surely know] the liars﴾ has already been discussed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us?﴾ The sayyi'ah (evil deed) is every trait whose consequence is bad, and the hasanah (good deed) is every trait whose consequence is pleasing.

His saying: ﴿that they can outrun Us﴾ means that they can escape Us. Whoever outstrips something has left it behind him. His saying: ﴿Evil is their judgment⁠—﴾ means: wretched is the judgment they make.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 5:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "Fears the meeting with Allah." Others said: "Hopes for (aml) the meeting with Allah." It was also said: the meeting with Allah is the meeting with His recompense, and it is said: the meeting with Allah is the return to Him on the Day of Resurrection.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, the term of Allah is coming﴾. Its meaning: indeed, the promise of Allah is coming. The ajal (term) is the appointed promise, and the meaning of the verse is: whoever fears or hopes, let him prepare himself. Makhul has narrated: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said, when this verse was revealed, to Ali and Fatimah: 'O Ali, and O Fatimah, Allah the Exalted has revealed His words: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾, so prepare yourselves.'" But the report is gharib (strange, weak in its chain).

And His words: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 6:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever strives, strives only for himself﴾. Jihad (striving, exertion) is patience in the face of hardship. Patience in the face of hardship may be in fighting, as the Sharia has commanded, and patience in the face of hardship may also be in opposing the self (nafs), in whatever sense that may be.

And His words: ﴿but he strives only for himself﴾ mean: the benefit of that returns to him.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ mean: no harm or benefit returns to Him from obedience or disobedience.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾. Takfir (expiation) is the removal of an evil deed by a good deed, and this is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾. Ihbat (nullification) is the removal of a good deed by an evil deed.

And His words: ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾. This is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof﴾. And its meaning: He will give them more than what they did, and better.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 8:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ mean: he should act kindly (ḥasanan). It was also read as iḥsānan (إحساناً), meaning: he should show kindness (yuḥsin iḥsānan).

And His words: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾ mean: do not obey them in disobeying Me. It is well known from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator."

And His words: ﴿that of which you have no knowledge﴾ He only said this because all shirk (associating partners with God) arises from ignorance, for the one who has knowledge does not associate partners with Allah.

And His words: ﴿To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾ are clear in meaning.

Most of the exegetes (mufassirūn) said that the verse was revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, who is Saʿd ibn Mālik Abū Isḥāq al-Zuhrī, and whose mother was Ḥamnah from the Banu Umayyah. It is narrated that when he embraced Islam — and he was among the earliest foremost (sābiqūn) in Islam — he was dutiful to his mother. When his mother heard of this, she summoned him and said to him: "What is this religion that you have innovated? By God, I will neither eat nor drink until you return from your religion or I die, and you will be disgraced with this for all time." Then she remained for one day and night without eating, and she became severely weakened. Then she remained another day and night without eating or drinking. Sa'd came to her and said: "O mother, even if you had a hundred souls and they departed one by one, I would not return from my religion." When she despaired of him, she ate and drank. And Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, commanding him to be dutiful to his parents and forbidding him to associate partners with Allah in obedience to them. It was also said: the verse is general in application.
The Exalted said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾, meaning: into the company of the righteous.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah.﴾ Meaning: he panics at the punishment of people just as one panics at the punishment of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you."﴾ The verse refers to the people who stayed behind in Mecca from among those who had embraced Islam. When the polytheists harmed them, they did not endure patiently, and they gave them what they demanded.

And His saying: ﴿victory from your Lord﴾ means: conquest from your Lord and a dominion for the believers.

And His saying: ﴿they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you"﴾ means: we were Muslims, and we were only coerced until we said what we said.

And His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾ Meaning: He knows what is in their breasts, so He distinguishes their truthfulness from their falsehood.

The Exalted said: ﴿And Allah will surely know those who believed, and He will surely know the hypocrites.﴾ We have already explained this. It is also said: "those who believed" means they fulfilled what they had pledged, and made their words true through their deeds. As for the hypocrites, they contradicted their words with their deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 12:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed﴾ It is related that Abu Sufyan and his kinsmen said to those who had embraced Islam: "Follow our way," that is, the path on which we are.

And His words: ﴿and we will carry your sins﴾ meaning: and we will carry your sins, if you fear His punishment; so we will stand surety for you and bear the punishment on your behalf.

And His words: ﴿But they will not carry anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars﴾ meaning: in their guarantee to bear the sins.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 13:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens﴾ mean: their sins (awzar), and awzar are the sins (dhunub).

And His words: ﴿and additional burdens along with their own burdens﴾ mean: additional sins along with their sins.

If it is said: How can this be consistent, when Allah the Exalted says in another verse: ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾? The answer to this is: the meaning of His words ﴿and additional burdens along with their own burdens﴾ is: the sin of their calling others to abandon faith. It is also said: the nobles among them [bear] the sins of the followers, because they established misguidance for them and called them to it. And it has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever calls to misguidance and is followed in it, upon him is the burden of whoever follows him, without that diminishing anything from their burdens."

And Abu Umamah al-Bahili narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection who has wronged this one, reviled this one, and taken the wealth of this one. His good deeds will be taken and given to them. It will be said: 'O Lord, there remain evil deeds upon him, and no good deeds remain for him.' Then Allah the Exalted will say: 'Carry their sins upon him.'" Then he recited the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens﴾, the verse.

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾ mean: what they used to lie about.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people﴾. It is narrated from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Noah was the first prophet sent to the people of the earth."

And His saying: ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Noah was sent when he was forty years old, and he remained after his coming out of the ship sixty years, and Allah, exalted is He, took him when he was a thousand and fifty years old. And in another narration: the lifespan of Noah was one thousand and four hundred [and fifty] [years], and he was sent when he was two hundred and fifty years old. And it has been said other than this, and Allah knows best.

It is also narrated that when the Angel of Death came to Noah to seize his soul, he said: "O the longest-lived of the prophets, how did you find the world?" He had a house with two doors, so he entered through one and exited through the other, and said: "Thus have I found it."

It is also narrated that he had a house of hair, and it was said to him: "If only you would build a house of clay." He would say: "I will die tomorrow, or I will die the day after tomorrow." So he departed the world upon that, and did not build a house.

If it is said: His saying, ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾, what is the benefit of the exception in this verse? Why did He not say: "So he remained among them nine hundred and fifty years"? The answer to this: the benefit of the exception is emphasis (ta'kid). For when the Arabs say: "Your brothers came to me," it is possible they mean all the brothers, and it is possible they mean most of them. But when one says: "Your brothers came to me except Zayd," you know with certainty that all the brothers came except Zayd. Thus the exception has conveyed emphasis in this respect. Some have said: Allah had made Noah's lifespan a thousand years, and he asked some of his sons for fifty years, and they granted them to him; then when the appointed time arrived, he sought the completion of the thousand but was not given it. So Allah mentioned it in the wording of an exception to indicate that the deficiency came from his side. This is a strange view.

And His saying: ﴿Then the flood seized them﴾. Al-tufan (the flood): everything abundant that encompasses a group, such as drowning, or death, or other than that. The rajiz (poet) said:

(Destroyed them a sweeping flood of death...)

And His saying: ﴿while they were wrongdoers﴾, i.e., polytheists.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 29, verse 15:

Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿So We saved him and the people of the ship﴾ — we have already explained the number of those who were in the ship.

And His saying: ﴿and made it a sign for the worlds﴾ — meaning: We made Our punishment of them by drowning a sign for the worlds. It is also said: We made the ship a sign for the worlds, for it remained cast upon al-Judi (Mount Judi) for a long period.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Abraham⦘ means: And We sent Abraham ﴿when he said to his people: Worship Allah and fear Him⦘, that is: obey Allah and beware of disobeying Him.

And His saying: ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew⦘ means: the worship of Allah and fear of Him is better for you, if you only knew. It has also been said that His saying ﴿Worship Allah⦘ means: declare Allah to be One (tawhid), and every instance of worship (ʿibadah) in the Qur'an carries the meaning of tawhid.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 17:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you worship besides Allah idols﴾ — meaning: idols (aṣnām).

And His words: ﴿and you invent a lie﴾ — meaning: you fabricate falsehood. Qatadah said: "﴿and you invent a lie﴾ — meaning: idols." The idols were called "a lie" (ifk) because they named them gods.

If it is said: He has said, "﴿and you create (takhluqūn)﴾," and He has said elsewhere, "﴿Is there any creator other than Allah?﴾" — meaning, there is no creator other than Allah. How then can the two verses be reconciled? The answer to this: "creating" (al-khalq) here carries the sense of "measuring/fashioning" (al-taqdīr). The poet said:

(And you indeed cut what you have fashioned... and some of the people fashion and then do not cut.)

It is also said: "﴿and you invent a lie﴾" means: you carve the idols with your hands and worship them. It is related that the Banu Hanifah made an idol of khays — which is dates with ghee — then a famine struck them and they ate it. The poet said:

(Hanifah ate its lord in the time of scorching and famine,)

(they did not fear from their Lord evil consequences and retribution.)

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision; so seek provision from Allah﴾ — meaning: so seek provision from Allah.

His words: ﴿and worship Him and give thanks to Him; to Him you will be returned﴾ — the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you deny, then indeed nations before you have denied﴾. They are such as ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ (Lot), and others.

And His saying: ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾. Its meaning: only the evident conveying (of the message).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 19:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it?﴾ If it is said: what is the meaning of His words ﴿Have they not seen﴾, when they have not seen the repetition (i'adah) of creation? The answer to this: the words ﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation﴾ form a complete sentence, and they used to acknowledge this. And His words ﴿then repeats it﴾ are the beginning of a new sentence. Some of them said: ﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation﴾ by the creation of the day, then repeats it by the coming of the night and the return of the day after it. This was related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Some of them said: ﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation﴾ by giving life, then repeats it for them by causing death and turning them into dust as they were.

And His words ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ mean: that is easy (hayyin).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 20:

The Most High's saying: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see how He originated creation﴾, meaning: how He created the creation.

And His saying: ﴿Then Allah brings about the final creation﴾. It has been recited as "al-nash'a al-akhira" (al-nash'ah al-ākhirah), and both have one meaning, like their saying: ra'fah and ra'āfah (both meaning "tenderness" or "compassion").

And His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾, meaning: over the first creation and the final creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wwills﴾ is clear in meaning. It is related from some of them: He punishes whom He wills through greed, and has mercy on whom He wills through contentment. It is also said: He punishes whom He wills through bad character, and has mercy on whom He wills through good character. And it is said: He punishes whom He wills through some people's enmity toward him, and has mercy on whom He wills through people's love for him.

And it is said: He punishes whom He wills through accepting innovation (bid'ah), and has mercy on whom He wills through steadfastly adhering to the Sunnah.

As for His saying: ﴿and to Him you will be turned back﴾, it means: you will be returned.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you cannot escape [Allah] in the earth or in the heaven﴾ (i.e., you cannot cause Allah to fail in [inflicting] His punishment upon you. Its meaning is that you will not escape Him as a person escapes what he is unable to overcome). If it is said: He said ﴿nor in the heaven﴾ while the address is to human beings, and they are not in the heaven, so how does this statement stand? The answer is in two ways. The first: ﴿And you cannot escape in the earth, nor is there any escape in the heaven.﴾ Al-Farra' said: "This is one of the obscure points of Arabic." Hassan ibn Thabit said in verse:

(And whoever of you satirizes the Messenger of Allah / and whoever praises him and supports him is equal)

That is: whoever of you praises him and supports him is equal [to the one who satirizes him in this regard, i.e., the verb is elided in the first clause]. The second answer: the meaning of His saying ﴿nor in the heaven﴾ is that even if you were in the heaven, you would not escape Him either, like a man who says: "You are not here to escape me, nor in Basra," meaning: even if you were in Basra, you would not escape me either.

And His saying: ﴿And you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾, i.e., any guardian or preventer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and His meeting﴾. Qatadah said: Allah censured peoples who were despised by Him, and He said: ﴿Those have despaired of My mercy, and for them is a painful punishment﴾. That is: painful, causing agony.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So the only answer of his people was that they said﴾. Know that the verses that came before are a parenthetical interruption in the story of Ibrahim, his calling his people to God and their reply to him, and those verses concern the Prophet and his disputation with the polytheists. Then the return to the reply of Ibrahim's people occurs in this verse.

And His words: ﴿"Kill him or burn him." But God delivered him from the fire.﴾ Mujahid said: The fire burned his bonds but did not burn him.

And His words: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ That is: who affirm (yusaddiqun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he said, "You have only taken idols besides Allah"﴾, meaning: idols (asnam). His saying: ﴿as an affection among yourselves﴾, meaning: it is an affection (mawaddah) among you, or: that is an affection among you in the life of this world. The meaning is that your brotherhood and mutual affection is specific to this world, and it ends when the Hereafter comes. It has also been said: every close friendship (khullah) will be severed on the Day of Resurrection except the close friendship of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun). It has been recited as "mawaddatan baynakum" in the accusative, with the verb falling upon it, meaning: you took them for the sake of affection. It has been recited otherwise as well, and the meanings are close to one another.

His saying: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others and curse one another﴾. The meaning of the plural is that disavowal occurs between the leaders and the followers.

His saying: ﴿And your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 26:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So Lut believed in him﴾. It is said that the lam (ل) may stand in the place of the ba' (ب), [so that the sense is "believed in him"].

And His words: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord"﴾, meaning: I am heading toward my Lord, seeking His pleasure. We have already explained that his emigration was from Kuthaa to al-Sham (Syria), and Kuthaa is a village in the region of al-Kufa. In the narrative: he emigrated after [fifty-five] years of his life had passed; and Lut and Sarah emigrated with him.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾, meaning: the Victorious in His affair, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ in His governance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 27:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Scripture﴾. It is said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not send any prophet after Abraham except from his lineage. If it is asked: Why did He not mention Ishmael, and mention Isaac and Jacob, while Ishmael was a prophet just as Isaac was? We say: Ishmael is included in His saying: ﴿and We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Scripture﴾. Furthermore, Allah the Exalted mentions some and omits others for brevity and conciseness, even though the meaning is one in all of them.

And His saying: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾, i.e., the good praise (al-thana' al-hasan).

Qatadah said: it is the acceptance of all the people of the religions of him and their approval of him. Al-Suddi said: it is the righteous offspring. It was also said: it is that his place in Paradise was shown to him. And it was said: that He made the prophets from among his descendants.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed he, in the Hereafter, is among the righteous﴾, i.e., among the company of the righteous.

Regarding His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has preceded you in."﴾ In the tafsir (exegesis) it is said that no male had mounted a male before the people of Lot,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you indeed approach men and cut off the way?﴾ That is, you approach men for the act of immorality. "And cut off the way" has two interpretations. The first: you cut off the path of procreation by preferring men over women.

The second view: "and cut off the way," meaning the road. They used to seize strangers and travelers and commit immorality with them.

His saying: ﴿And commit the evil deed in your gatherings?﴾ The nadi (gathering place, assembly) is the majlis (sitting place, council). As for the evil deed they committed, there are several views. The first: it is the commission of immorality by men in their assemblies, related by Mujahid.

It is related from A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: they would break wind at one another among themselves. It is related from Abdullah ibn Salam: some of them would spit on others. And in some reports traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ): "They used to sit on the road, pelt people with pebbles, and mock them."

It is related from some of them that it was whistling, shooting with the jalahiq (a crossbow-like pellet launcher), playing with pigeons, showing off in the road, and loosening their waistwraps.

His saying: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful."﴾ That is, in what you say.
His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, help me against the corrupting people."﴾ Their corruption is as we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 31:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Ibrahim with the good tidings﴾ — we have already explained the meaning of al-bushra (good tidings) in Surah Hud.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We are going to destroy the people of this town﴾ — meaning Sodom. In the narrative: they used to sit, and in front of each of them was a bowl (qa'b) containing pebbles. When a person passed by them, each of them would flick (khadhafa) a pebble at him, and whoever hit him had the better claim to him. So he would take what was with him, have intercourse with him, and fine him three dirhams. And they had a judge who would rule accordingly.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers﴾ — we have already explained their wrongdoing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 32:

The words of the Most High: ﴿He said, "Indeed, Lut is therein." They said, "We are most knowing of who is therein."﴾ That is: the angels said, "We are most knowing of who is therein."

And His words: ﴿We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she was of those who remain behind﴾ That is: those who remained in the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 33:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account﴾. That is: he was distressed by the angels. Its meaning is that the coming of the angels as guests displeased him, because he knew the wickedness of his people.

And His saying: ﴿and he felt constrained for them﴾. That is: he was constrained (dhar‘an, lit. "his arm-span") by their coming. It is said: "So-and-so was constrained by such-and-such" when he disliked it.

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not fear, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is among those who remain behind."﴾ "Do not fear for us from your people, and do not grieve over our destroying them."

And His saying: ﴿"Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife, who was among those who remained (al-ghabirin)"﴾. That is: those who remained behind in the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We are sending down upon the people of this town﴾, meaning: Sodom (Sadūm).

And His saying: ﴿a punishment from the sky﴾, meaning: a punishment from the sky.

And His saying: ﴿because they used to defy﴾, meaning: they used to disobey.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 35:

His saying: ﴿And We have left from it a clear sign﴾, meaning: from the towns of the people of Lut.

Qatadah said: The clear sign is (the stones with which they were destroyed, and some of them had remained until the earliest of this community reached them). Mujahid said: The clear sign is the appearance of the black water from their towns.

And His saying: ﴿for a people who use their reason﴾, meaning: who reflect upon the signs with the reflection of people of intellect.

And to Madyan (We sent) their brother Shu'ayb. Its meaning: and We sent to Madyan their brother Shu'ayb.

And His saying: ﴿So he said, "O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day"﴾. That is: and fear the Last Day. It is also said: the "rajā'" (hope) is in its true sense, which is expectation.

And His saying: ﴿And do not commit abuse in the land, spreading corruption﴾. That is: do not cause corruption in the land. [Al-'ayth] is the most severe corruption.

"And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So they denied him, and the earthquake seized them﴾. Al-rajfah (the violent quaking): a shaking that leads to destruction."

"And His saying: ﴿So they woke in their homes, prostrate﴾, meaning: dead. It was also said: extinguished (lifeless)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 38:

Allah the Exalted's statement: ﴿And [We destroyed] ʿAd and Thamud﴾, meaning: and We destroyed ʿAd and Thamud.

And His statement: ﴿And it has become clear to you from their dwellings﴾, meaning: the abodes in which they lived.

And His statement: ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear fair to them and barred them from the way﴾, meaning: he barred them from the way of truth.

And His statement: ﴿while they were discerning﴾, meaning: they committed what they committed while they knew that the outcome of their affair would be ruin.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 39:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Qarun and Pharaoh and Haman﴾, meaning: And We destroyed Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman. It is mentioned in the tafsir of al-Naqqash that Pharaoh used to sell melons at the beginning of his affair, and Haman was a brick-maker (ṭayyān).

And His saying: ﴿And Moses had come to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning: with evident signs (dalālāt).

His saying: ﴿But they were arrogant in the land, and they were not ones who could escape﴾, meaning: they were not ones who could get away from Our punishment, like one who outruns something and so it has escaped him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 40:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So each one We seized for his sin⦆. That is: We seized each of these people for their sin.

And His saying: ﴿Among them are those upon whom We sent a hasib (hāṣib)﴾. The hāṣib (a violent wind bearing pebbles) is the wind that carries the hasbā' (ḥaṣbā'), and the ḥaṣbā' is small stones (pebbles). Those who were destroyed by the pebbles were the people of Lut (Lot).

And His saying: ﴿And among them are those who were seized by the Cry﴾. He means the people of Salih, who were the Thamud.

And His saying: ﴿And among them are those whom We caused the earth to swallow﴾. That is Qarun (Korah).

And His saying: ﴿And among them are those whom We drowned﴾. That refers to the people of Nuh (Noah) and the people of Fir'awn (Pharaoh).

And His saying: ﴿And Allah was not one to wrong them﴾. That is: Allah did not wrong them. ﴿But they wronged themselves.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 41:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah﴾. Al-mathal (the parable, likeness): a saying that circulates widely and contains a comparison of the state of one thing with the state of another.

His words: ﴿protectors﴾, meaning: the idols.

His words: ﴿like the spider's (ankabut)﴾. The ankabut (spider) is a creature to which Allah, exalted is He, gave an instrument with which it weaves a house to shelter in, and its house is in the utmost weakness and frailty. The reason the worship of idols is likened to the spider's house is that the spider's house protects from neither heat nor cold, and likewise the worship of idols brings no benefit and repels no harm.

Some reports state that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The spider is a transformed devil, so kill it." But the report is gharib (strange, weak in its transmission).

And it is related from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he ordered that the spider's web not be left in the house, and said: "Leaving it brings poverty." We have already explained that Allah, exalted is He, made the spider a soldier of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the cave.

His words: ﴿Indeed, the frailest of houses is the spider's house, if only they knew﴾, meaning: if only they knew that the worship of idols avails nothing, just as they know that the spider's house repels nothing.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke besides Him of anything﴾, i.e., He knows what they invoke besides Him, namely the idols and others.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, i.e., the Mighty in exacting retribution from His enemies, the Wise in the management of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 43:

Allah's words: ﴿And these parables We present to the people﴾, meaning: the likenesses by which the comparison is made.

And His words: ﴿but none understands them except those who have knowledge﴾ (meaning: those who have knowledge of the meanings of My speech). It is related from one of the early generations (al-salaf) that he said: It is recommended to pause at every parable in the Qur'an, for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿but none understands them except those who have knowledge﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 44:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, i.e., with wisdom.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers﴾, i.e., a lesson (ʿibrah) for the believers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 45:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾ means: the Quran.

And His saying: ﴿Establish the prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing﴾. Al-fahsha' (immorality) is every ugly act, and al-munkar (wrongdoing) is everything that the Shari'ah disapproves of. (If it is said: how does He say "Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing," when we have seen someone who prays and yet does not refrain from immorality and wrongdoing? We say: it is related from Hammad ibn Salamah that he said: it prohibits immorality and wrongdoing for as long as one is in the prayer, and from others: it prohibits immorality and wrongdoing) during it and after it. The meaning of the prohibition according to this view is that when one recites the Quran and recites it, it forbids him from immorality and wrongdoing.

It is related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: There is no prayer for one who does not obey the prayer. In this wording there is an indication of what we have explained.

In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) it is stated: "Whoever his prayer does not restrain from immorality and wrongdoing, it has increased him in distance from Allah only."

(45) ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a manner that is best, except for those of them who have wronged, and say: "We believe..."﴾

It is related from al-Hasan and Qatadah that they both said: whoever prays and does not desist from immorality and wrongdoing, his prayer is a burden upon him.

And His saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ has two interpretations. One of them: the remembrance of Allah is more excellent than all acts of obedience. It is related from Thabit al-Bunani that a man freed four slaves, and another person kept remembering Allah with tasbih, tahmid and tahlil. Then a group of people of knowledge were asked about that, and they said: the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He, is more excellent, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾.

The second view is that its meaning is: the remembrance of Allah of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas. It is related that a man said to Ibn 'Abbas: so-and-so says concerning His saying ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ that its meaning is: when one remembers Him and refrains from His disobediences. He said: this is a good statement, but it is not the meaning of the verse; the meaning of the verse is what we have mentioned from him, namely: the remembrance of Allah of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. Some of them said: the remembrance of Allah in reward is greater than your remembrance of Him in obedience.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah knows what you do﴾ means: what you do.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 46:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions.

The first: "And do not argue with the People of the Book" — those who have accepted the jizya (poll-tax) — "except in a way that is best." His words "except those of them who have done wrong" refer, according to this opinion, to the people of war (ahl al-harb).

The second opinion: "And do not argue with the People of the Book" means: those of them who believed. The meaning of the prohibition against arguing with them after their faith is that they used to report things in their books that the believers did not know, so [He] forbade arguing with them about these matters, since they might be true.

His words "except those of them who have done wrong" refer to those who did not believe. It is related from Qatadah that he said: the verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by the verse of the sword.

His words: ﴿And say: We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you﴾. (It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "When the People of the Book inform you of something you do not know, do not believe them and do not deny them, but say: ﴿We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you; our God and your God is One, and to Him we are submitting﴾.")

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have sent down to you the Book﴾, meaning: just as We sent you with the truth, We sent down to you the Book.

And His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book believe in it﴾, meaning: they affirm it. And His saying: ﴿And among these there are those who believe in it﴾, meaning: and among the polytheists there are those who affirm it. So His saying ﴿these﴾ is a reference to the polytheists who were in Makkah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers﴾, the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 48:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And you did not recite before it any book﴾, meaning: before We sent you (as a messenger) and sent down the Qur'an to you.

And His words: ﴿nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, meaning: you were not one who reads or writes.

And His words: ﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had doubt﴾, meaning: otherwise the disbelievers would have doubted if you had read and written. As for the people of polytheism, they used to claim that he had read from the books of the ancients and copied from them. As for the People of the Book, it was among the descriptions of him in their books that he was an unlettered prophet who neither reads nor writes; so if he had read and written, doubt would have fallen upon them.

It is related from al-Sha'bi that he said: The Prophet did not leave this world until he had written and read. But this is a weak view that should not be relied upon, and [I think] it is not authentically reported from al-Sha'bi, for he was a great scholar.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 49:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾. That is: the Qur'an is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. It is also said that its meaning is: Muhammad is one possessing clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge. It is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "God Most High said to me: I sent you to test you and to test others through you, and I sent down to you a Book which water cannot wash away; you recite it while asleep and while awake." This refers to what we have explained, that the Qur'an is in the breasts of the believers, and nothing can abrogate it or wash it away.

And His words: ﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers﴾. That is: the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 50:

His words: ﴿They say: Why has not a sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?﴾ That is: like what was sent down upon ʿIsa (Jesus) of the table spread (al-Ma'idah), and what was given to Salih of the she-camel, and to Musa of the hand and the staff. ﴿Say: The signs are only with Allah﴾ That is: the signs are with Allah; He gives them by His will and His decree.

And His words: ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾ We have already explained it. Know that Allah, exalted is He, has given His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) many miracles, but He did not give him according to what they proposed, and they used to demand that the signs conform to their suggestions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 51:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them﴾. Al-kifayah (sufficiency): reaching an end (ghayah) that removes need.

And His saying: ﴿That We have sent down to you the Book﴾, meaning: the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿Being recited to them﴾, meaning: being read to them.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is mercy﴾, meaning: a blessing for those who believe in it.

And His saying: ﴿And a reminder﴾, meaning: an admonition and a reminding. We have already explained the aspect of its inimitability (i'jaz) in the Qur'an in terms of its arrangement (nazm), its meaning, its reports of the unseen, and other things.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 52:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Allah suffices as a witness between me and you.﴾ Shahadah (testimony): an report about something witnessed, upon which a legal ruling is built. Allah the Exalted is a witness over the actions of the believers and the disbelievers alike.

And His saying: ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

And His saying: ﴿And those who believe in falsehood﴾ means: in other than Allah. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The truest word spoken by the Arabs is the saying of Labid:

(Surely everything other than Allah is false, and every bliss is certainly going to perish.)

Then he said: Except the bliss of Paradise."

Know that when faith (iman) is stated without qualification, what is meant is faith in Allah. When it is qualified, it is permissible to say: he believed in Iblis, he believed in the taghut, and what is similar to that. This is like when it is said: so-and-so is standing (qa'im), and it is stated without qualification while meaning one who is characterized by it. When it is said, it is permissible to say: standing with the management, standing with the kingship. Yahya ibn Salam said: "The falsehood here is Iblis."

And His saying: ﴿And disbelieved in Allah﴾ means: they denied Allah.

And His saying: ﴿It is they who are the losers.﴾ The losers (al-khasirun) are those who have lost their capital. Since the disbelievers did an act by which they exposed themselves to destruction, Allah named them losers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 53:

Allah's saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾. We have already explained that al-Nadr ibn al-Harith said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾, and the verse [continues]. This is the hastening for the punishment.

As for His saying: ﴿And were it not for a specified term﴾, it means the promised Day of Resurrection. It has also been said: the blowing into the Trumpet. And it is said: the appointed time for their punishment.

As for His saying: ﴿the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come upon them suddenly﴾, meaning unexpectedly, ﴿while they do not perceive﴾, meaning they do not know of its coming.

In the narration of Abu Hurayrah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a man will lift his morsel and will not put it into his mouth before the Hour is established."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment﴾. It is said: what is meant by it is what is meant by the first verse; he repeated it for emphasis. And it is said: this verse was revealed concerning a people of ignorant folk of this community. The first opinion is more preferable.

His saying: ﴿And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾, that is: it gathers their punishment. And it is said its meaning is: they must certainly enter it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them﴾. He means: the punishment will befall them from above them and from beneath their feet. It is like His saying, exalted is He, in another verse: ﴿They will have above them canopies of fire, and beneath them canopies﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And it will be said, "Taste what you used to do."﴾ We have already explained the meaning of tasting (dhawq) earlier.

And His saying: ﴿what you used to do﴾, i.e., as recompense for what you used to do.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said concerning this verse: "They used to leave a land when disobedience (al-ma'siyah) appeared in it." And it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ata' that they both said: "When you are commanded to disobedience in a town (baldah), then leave it." (And in another narration: "When disobedience appears in a town, then leave it.")

The scholars (ahl al-'ilm) have mentioned that if one is unable to enjoin good (al-amr bil-ma'ruf) and forbid evil (al-nahy 'an al-munkar), he should also leave. The verse was revealed concerning a people who stayed behind from the emigration (hijrah) in Makkah, and they said: "We fear that if we emigrate we will suffer hunger and hardship in livelihood." So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse, and He did not excuse them for not leaving. There is another view concerning the verse: that the meaning of His saying ﴿indeed My earth is spacious﴾ is that My provision is spacious; this was mentioned by Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir.

As for His saying ﴿so worship Me alone﴾, it means: make Me One (wahhiduni) and obey Me.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 57:

His saying: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ means: your leaving them (from) the migration does not save them from death. It has been narrated by Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) that when the Prophet (ﷺ) passed away, they heard the sound of a person but did not see him, and he said: "Peace be upon you, O People of the House, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ [and so on, to the end of the verse]. Indeed, in Allah there is consolation for every calamity, a substitute for everyone who perishes, and a recompense for everything that is lost. Truly, in Allah put your trust, and to Him turn your hope, for the one truly afflicted is the one deprived of the reward."

His saying: ﴿Then to Us you will be returned﴾ means: you will be brought back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 58:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise﴾ meaning: We will surely make them dwell in Paradise in lofty chambers, that is, high mansions. Abu Malik al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has chambers in Paradise, whose outsides can be seen from their insides and whose insides can be seen from their outsides." It was said: "For whom are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "For those who speak kindly, feed the food, and pray at night while people are sleeping."

It has been recited as "lanuthwiyannahum" (لنثوينهم), and al-thawa (الثوى) is residence, while al-tabawwu' (التبوؤ) is alighting in the place where one dwells. In the reports of the Jahiliyyah it is related that al-Muhalhil, when he killed the son of al-Harith ibn Abbad in the war between Bakr and Taghlib, said: "He has taken up residence (tabawwa') for the thong of Kulayb's sandal."

And it is well known from al-Husayn that he said to al-Hasan concerning the killing of Abu Lu'lu'ah (Ibn Muljam): "Do not make him dwell (thawa) with our father," meaning: do not make him alight in the station of our father.

As for the words: ﴿Beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ meaning: the workers of obedience.

**Al-Sam'ani's Commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 29, Verse 59:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿[Those] who endured patiently and put their trust in their Lord﴾, meaning: they endured patiently upon ( ﴿59﴾ ) And how many a creature does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ the hardships. And His saying: ﴿and put their trust in their Lord﴾, meaning: they rely upon Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 29, verse 60:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾ meaning: and how many an animal that crawls upon the earth.

And His words: ﴿does not carry its provision﴾ meaning: does not carry its provision with it. It has also been said: it does not store up its provision for the morrow.

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and the well-known report from Sufyan al-Thawri: "There is no animal that stores something up for the morrow except the son of Adam, the mouse, the ant, and the magpie (al-'aqta')." Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that what is meant by His words, ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾, is Muhammad: he did not store anything up for the morrow. And it is established by the narration of Anas: "The Prophet did not store anything up for the morrow."

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: This hadith was related to us by Abu Mansur Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Nisaburi in Baghdad, from his own recitation, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Khaffaf informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Sarraj informed us, from Qutayba, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i, from Thabit, from Anas ... the report.

In some reports, through the narration of Ibn 'Umar, he said: "I went with the Messenger of Allah, and he was picking up dates and eating them, and I nearly did not eat them. He said to me: 'Will you not eat it, O Ibn 'Umar?' I said: 'I have no desire for it.' He said: 'But I have a desire for it. This is the fourth morning of forty days, and I have not tasted food. If I asked Allah, He would give me the like of the kingdom of Kisra and Caesar.' Then he said: 'How will it be with you, O Ibn 'Umar, when you remain among a people who store up provision for their year, and certainty weakens?' He said: 'We did not leave that place until Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾.'" And the report is strange (gharib).

And His words: ﴿Allah provides for it and for you﴾ mean: He provides for that creature and for you.

And His words: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: its meaning is apparent. And among what is well known from the Prophet is that he said: "If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, you would be provided for as the bird is provided for: it goes out in the morning hungry and returns in the evening full."

And it is also well known that he, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) breathed into my heart that no soul will die until it has fully received its provision. So fear Allah and seek provision in a good manner."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?"﴾ That is, "and subjected (dhallala) the sun and the moon."

And His saying: ﴿They will surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾ That is, they are turned away (yusrafun) from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 62:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah extends provision to whomever He wills of His servants, and restricts it for him﴾ means: He grants abundance to whomever He wills, and constricts it for whomever He wills.

As for His statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 63:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and with it gives life to the earth after its death?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah."﴾ That is: for the Doer of these things is Allah.

And His words: ﴿But most of them do not reason﴾, meaning: they do not know that the Doer of these things is Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 64:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play﴾. Al-lahw (diversion) is enjoying the pleasures of this world, and it is called lahw because it is perishing, unlike the pleasures of the Hereafter.

His saying: ﴿And play﴾, meaning and frivolity (al-ʿabath). It is said that it was called lahw and la'ib only because it is engaged in by those who do not reflect upon the consequences.

His saying: ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter – that is the [true] life﴾, meaning: that is the everlasting life. The scholars of language said: al-hayawan and al-hayah (life) have the same meaning; this is related from Abu ʿUbayda and Abu [ʿAmr]. The meaning of the verse is that in the Hereafter there is everlasting life.

His saying: ﴿If they only knew﴾, meaning: if they only knew that the world perishes and the Hereafter endures.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 65:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So when they board a ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾ That is: they call upon Allah and abandon calling upon the idols. It is related from ʿIkrima, who said: "If they were riding the sea and carrying their idols with them, then when the sea became rough and they feared drowning, they threw their idols into the sea, and they would say: 'O Lord, O Lord!'"

And His words: ﴿But when He delivers them to the land, behold, they associate partners with Him.﴾ That is: they returned to what they had been upon.

Translation:

"And His saying: ﴿So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them, and so that they may enjoy themselves; but they will come to know﴾ is in the manner of a threat."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 67:

And His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We have made a sanctuary secure⁠—﴾ meaning: a place of security (dhā amn). And His saying: ﴿while people are being snatched away from around them﴾: al-ikhtiṭāf (snatching away) is the seizing of something swiftly, and we have already explained this meaning before.

And His saying: ﴿Will they then believe in falsehood?﴾ meaning: will they believe in other than God? It is an interrogative expression carrying the sense of denunciation (inkār).

And His saying: ﴿and in the blessing of God do they disbelieve?﴾ meaning: they deny it (yajḥadūn).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 29, verse 68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, meaning: he who lies against Allah and claims that He has sent down what He has not sent down.

And His saying: ﴿or denies the truth when it has come to him﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. It was also said: Muhammad (ﷺ).

And His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾, meaning: an abode and a place of settlement for the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 29, verse 69:

The words of God Most High: ﴿And those who strive in Our cause﴾. It is narrated from al-Hasan that he said: "The best jihad is opposing one's desire (hawa)." It is also said: "Jihad here is acting upon what one has come to know." And it is narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri that he said to Ibrahim ibn Adham: "Will you not come to us so that you may learn from us?" He said: "I have heard two hadiths, and when I have finished with them, I will learn the third." Then it is narrated with a chain (isnad) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever renounces the world, God illuminates his heart."

It is also said: mujahadah (striving) is patience upon acts of obedience and abstaining from acts of disobedience. It is also said: fighting the disbelievers. It is also said: realizing sincerity (ikhlas) in deeds, and this is the reality of God Most High's words: ﴿in Us﴾.

As for His words: ﴿We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾, meaning: We will increase them in guidance. It is also said: We will guide them to the straight (ways), and the straight ways are those that lead to the pleasure of God Most High. It is narrated from Ibn al-Mubarak that he said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said to me: "When people differ, then hold to what he said to the people of jihad and the frontier posts, for God Most High says: ﴿And those who strive in Our cause, We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾."

As for His words: ﴿And indeed, God is with the doers of good﴾, meaning: with support and aid.
